newsitem.title: UK: British output prices fall 0.1 percent in March.
newsitem.headline: British output prices fall 0.1 percent in March.

text.p: British output prices fell by 0.1 percent in March after a 0.1 percent monthly fall in February, the Office for National Statistics said on Monday.
Output, or factory gate, prices rose by 1.0 percent year-on-year in March after a 1.2 percent year-on-year rise the previous month.

The figures were better than expected and likely to be seized on by the ruling Conservative Party, seeking to overcome a large opposition Labour Party lead in opinion polls ahead of the May 1 election.
The Conservatives have sought, with limited success so far, to highlight what they say is Britain's strong economic performance under their leadership.
Input prices fell a seasonally adjusted 0.5 percent in March and dropped an unadjusted 7.6 percent year-on-year.
Chris Tinker, Chief Treasury Economist at Standard Chartered, said: "The overall balance of the numbers has come in at the positive end of any expectations."
